If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.50) in the last 3 days, apply a 2% asymmetric correction: +2% if sentiment rises, -2% if sentiment falls, applied mid-horizon (days 11–20).  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >1.5% from recent 7-day average, apply a 1% correction in mid-horizon to align with sentiment inertia.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is trending downward, reverse the last 3 forecast points by +0.5–1.0% to counteract sentiment-overlooked momentum.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is trending upward, reduce the last 3 forecast points by +0.5–1.0% to prevent sentiment-mismatched overcorrection.
